standard_prerequisites.name: Cauchy reals and their limits
standard_prerequisites.statement: RC is generated by rational points and by limits of Cauchy approximations, and closeness is the generated relation on them.
standard_prerequisites.use: The proof inducts on RC and uses two of the closeness constructors explicitly.

standard_prerequisites.name: Roundedness and triangle inequality for closeness
standard_prerequisites.statement: closeness is rounded and satisfies the triangle inequality.
standard_prerequisites.use: They are used at source lines 1351-1352.

core_obligations: Rational case: if u is a rational point the claim is exactly the second constructor of the closeness relation (source line 1346).
Limit case: assume the statement for each x_eta and, taking y := x and delta := eta in that assumption, deduce x_eta close-(eta + theta) lim(x) for all eta, theta (source lines 1347-1348).

For arbitrary y, epsilon, delta with lim(x) close-epsilon y_delta, use roundedness to get theta with lim(x) close-(epsilon - theta) y_delta, then combine with the previous observation and the triangle inequality to get x_eta close-(epsilon + eta - theta/2) y_delta (source lines 1350-1352).
Apply the fourth constructor of closeness to obtain lim(x) close-(epsilon + 2 eta + delta - theta/2) lim(y), and choose eta := theta/4 (source lines 1353-1354).

proof_roadmap.step: Induct on the Cauchy reals; rational case by a constructor.
Specialize the inductive hypothesis to obtain the auxiliary closeness.
Roundedness, triangle inequality and the choice of eta.

difficulty_reason: Counted unit is Lemma 11.3.36 at source lines 1341-1343: if u is close to y_delta within epsilon then u is close to the limit of y within epsilon + delta. The author's proof (source lines 1344-1355) is a genuine induction on the Cauchy reals whose limit case needs three separate ingredients: the inductive hypothesis is first specialised by taking y := x and delta := eta to obtain a family of closeness statements about lim(x) (lines 1347-1348), then roundedness is used to shave the parameter and the triangle inequality to combine the two closenesses (lines 1350-1352), and the fourth constructor of the relation is applied before an arithmetic choice of eta := theta/4 closes the estimate (lines 1353-1354). The statement records none of the auxiliary closeness or of the choice of eta.
